think: The organizing invariant of this monograph is a three-way taxonomy — unsupervised/generative, supervised/discriminative, and hybrid deep networks (PDF pp. 24-26) — and the hybrid class exists for a precise, printed reason: unsupervised learning assists discrimination through exactly two channels, optimization and regularization. The optimization viewpoint is that generative pre-training supplies excellent initialization points in a highly non-convex parameter landscape; the regularization viewpoint is that it supplies a prior on the set of representable functions (PDF pp. 36-37, citing the Erhan et al. analysis). Everything technical in Chapters 4-6 is an instance of making one of those channels tractable. The RBM is the engine of the optimization channel: an energy-based joint distribution (p1) whose bipartite restriction factorizes the conditionals into per-unit sigmoids (p2), which makes block Gibbs sampling exact and cheap, which in turn makes the contrastive-divergence gradient — data correlations minus model correlations (p3) — computable at all. The partition function is intractable, so the entire generative program is an approximation program, and the source is honest about where the approximations fail: CD is a pre-training tool, and persistent CD works better when the RBM must actually generate (PDF p. 54). The DSN takes the opposite route to tractability: instead of approximating a non-convex objective, it restructures the architecture so that each module's output-weight subproblem is convex and closed-form, U = (H H^T)^{-1} H T^T (p4), an ordinary-least-squares projection that enables batch-mode, parallelizable learning; the tensor variant shifts more of the non-convex burden into the convex U-step, and the kernel variant eliminates W-learning entirely (PDF pp. 66-71). Read together, these are one recurring move: convert a non-convex learning problem into convex or tractable subproblems — greedy layer-wise pre-training, closed-form output weights, the kernel trick, and later dropout as implicit model averaging (p6). The second deep lesson is that every method's validity is regime-conditional. Pre-training is most prominent when labeled data are limited (PDF p. 154); with abundant labels, discriminative pre-training or even careful random initialization plus SGD works as well or better (PDF pp. 19, 57), and the conclusion states flatly that DBN pre-training 'appears unnecessary if enough data and computing power are used' (PDF p. 156). The macro-level evidence is the scaling table (p7): as training data grow from hours to thousands of hours, the DNN's relative error reduction over the GMM-HMM baseline grows from roughly ten to twenty to thirty percent, while computation scales almost linearly. The honest extraction therefore keeps two layers separate: the durable mathematical kernels (energy model, factorized conditionals, contrastive gradient, least-squares projection, dropout, ReLU) and the era-bound empirical claims (2010-2013 WER tables, ImageNet error rates, the pre-training debate). The kernels transfer to any latent-state modeling problem; the numbers transfer only as historical calibration anchors. A simulator stack that confuses the two — treating a 2012 benchmark as a law, or a regime-conditional trick as a universal recipe — violates the source's own most repeated warning: no single deep learning technique succeeds for all tasks (PDF p. 155).

The repeated insistence that pre-training 'appears unnecessary if enough data and computing power are used' (PDF p. 156) is the authors negotiating with their own 2009 legacy: they know the DBN story that made the field famous is being superseded by scale, and they write the correction into their own conclusion before critics do.

Speech spectrograms become 312-bit binary codes through a deep autoencoder, reconstructing more faithfully than a 312-bit vector quantizer (PDF pp. 43-45); documents become 128-bit semantic hashes retrieved by Hamming distance (PDF pp. 120-121); words leave 1-of-V symbolic coding for low-dimensional continuous embeddings (PDF pp. 104, 109); queries and documents meet in a shared semantic space scored by cosine similarity (p5); images are projected into the text-embedding space for zero-shot recognition (PDF pp. 143-144). The second invariant is objective alignment. On page 74 the Q-learning update is printed explicitly: Q(state, action) = (1 - learning_rate) * Q(state, action) + learning_rate * Q_target, with Q_target = reward + discount_factor * max_{action'} Q(state', action'). I identified learning_rate with alpha and discount_factor with gamma, and noted that the max backup makes Q-learning off-policy: it targets the greedy policy regardless of the behavior policy. The greedy policy itself, policy: state -> argmax_{action} Q(state, action), is the decision rule that turns the learned value function into action. On page 98 the deep Q-network loss is given in code: q_target_sa = rew_ph + discount_factor * q_target_max and error = tf.reduce_sum(tf.square(q_target_sa - q_current_sa)). This is the least-squares Bellman residual, the squared temporal-difference error, minimized by gradient descent. The crucial subtlety is that the target is bootstrapped from the network's own estimates, making this a semi-gradient method subject to the deadly triad of function approximation, bootstrapping and off-policy learning, which can diverge without target networks or experience replay. The sovereign insight connecting these three is delayed reward assignment: the source repeatedly uses Space Invaders, where the player is rewarded when an alien explodes rather than when the player shoots, yet the shoot action is the true cause. The Bellman backup propagates reward backward through time so the earlier action receives credit. Dimensionally, Q-values and rewards are in dimensionless game-score units, alpha and gamma are dimensionless in [0,1], and the squared TD loss is in score-units squared. Breakdown regimes: constant alpha prevents convergence, gamma=1 in continuing tasks gives unbounded returns, the max operator induces overestimation bias under noise, and partial observability (raw pixels) breaks the Markov assumption — which is why the source stacks frames. The source also makes the exploration-exploitation tradeoff explicit: exploration means the agent acts randomly, exploitation means it uses its Q-values to choose the action it believes optimal, and the agent must balance the two to avoid premature convergence on a suboptimal policy. This is the same exploration burden GSE faces when evaluating novel play calls against an adapting defense rather than always exploiting the highest-EPA call, and it is why a purely greedy policy is insufficient in a non-stationary strategic environment.

think: The statistical-learning primitives come from two chapters. On page 119 (repeated on page 113) the least-squares agent computes the ridge-regression closed form in code: newW = np.linalg.inv(X.T.dot(X) + 10e-4 * I).dot(X.T.dot(y)), then interpolates W = w_lr * newW + (1 - w_lr) * W. This is Tikhonov-regularized least squares, W = (X^T X + lambda I)^{-1} X^T y with lambda = 10e-4 = 0.001, used as a linear Q-function approximator Q(s) = s.dot(W). The lambda I term guarantees invertibility even when X^T X is rank-deficient, which matters for one-hot state features where unseen states make the Gram matrix singular. The exponential-moving-average interpolation stabilizes successive closed-form fits across episodes. On page 108 the bias-variance decomposition is stated in prose: the decomposition is a breakdown of true error into bias and variance, where true error is mean squared error, the expected difference between predicted and true labels. I formalized this as E[(y - f-hat)^2] = Bias^2 + Variance + sigma^2, noting honestly that the source emphasizes two components while the irreducible noise term completes the identity. The accompanying claim that increasing model complexity increases sample complexity exponentially is a heuristic illustrated by the FrozenLake observation that adding a network layer quadruples the required episodes, not a theorem with a universal exponent. On page 49 cross-entropy (log-loss) is described as quantifying the difference between two probability distributions, zero for perfect classification, minimized by gradient descent taking steps along the negative gradient, with Adam adding momentum via an exponentially weighted average of gradients. I formalized categorical cross-entropy H(p,q) = -sum p(c) log q(c) and the gradient-descent update. Dimensionally, ridge weights carry target-units per feature-unit, lambda matches the Gram-matrix diagonal units (dimensionless for one-hot features), MSE is in label-units squared, and cross-entropy is in dimensionless information units. Breakdown regimes: ridge becomes ill-conditioned as lambda approaches zero with collinear features and overshrinks for large lambda; the bias-variance identity is specific to squared loss and the classical U-shaped curve can break under double descent; cross-entropy diverges for overconfident wrong predictions and gradient descent only guarantees local minima. The classifier chapter's Naive Bayes and the intro chapter's discussion of bias are conceptual and social respectively, so I did not extract them as mathematical primitives — the intro's bias is human bias, not statistical bias. I mapped ridge to GSE's regularized linear EPA models, bias-variance to GSE's complexity-versus-data tradeoff, and cross-entropy to GSE outcome classification, each with concrete telemetry. The unifying thesis of the chapter is that the least-squares agent, being a simpler linear model, should solve FrozenLake with fewer training episodes than the deep Q-network, directly instantiating the bias-variance tradeoff: lower model complexity reduces sample complexity at the cost of higher bias. This is precisely the lever GSE pulls when choosing between a parsimonious linear EPA model and a data-hungry nonlinear alternative, and the source's closing question — whether a high-performing agent can be trained with far fewer samples — is the same sample-efficiency question that governs model selection under a limited tracking-data budget.
theory_of_mind: The authors intend to equip developers with practical, reproducible projects, so they favor closed-form and library solutions over derivations. The least-squares agent is presented as a deliberate simplification to reduce sample complexity, modeling the reader as someone who wants a working bot with less compute. The social-bias section models the reader as an ethical actor who must audit data and teams, not just algorithms.

That ratio is a hazard gate, not a cause: a sudden spike relative to the rolling month raises soft-tissue injury probability. In parallel, the same session is observed through a subjective channel, the session rating of perceived exertion multiplied by session time (553c5528787d2538:p2, p. 19), and through an autonomic channel, the morning lnRMSSD vagal index (553c5528787d2538:p6, pp. 20-21). The injury date anchors the acute window; the month before it defines chronic exposure; the 3-day or 7-day lag choice (p1 EWMA variant, p. 20) decides which load spike is even visible. This backward anchoring is a selection bias built into the metric: we only ever compute the ratio for players who got hurt, so the ratio's apparent predictive power is partly an artifact of conditioning on the outcome. The derived kernel therefore carries two state variables per player, an external-load ratio and an internal-recovery residual, and transitions to the injured/removed state when either crosses its gate, with the internal gate dominating for linemen. The recursive clash is that each model of the others' incentives distorts the signal: the coach suspects the scientist of over-caution, the scientist suspects the player of masking fatigue, and the lineman's culture of playing through soreness biases the subjective channel. The population medians are deceptively calm: a median peak linear acceleration of 20.5 g and rotational acceleration of 1400 rad/s^2 for everyday impacts (553c5528787d2538:p3, p. 8), rising to 66.7 g and 2963 rad/s^2 for mild traumatic brain injury. A naive model would set a threshold somewhere between and classify hits. The review explicitly forbids this: concussion is a complex multidimensional event depending on impact location, frequency, head posture, neck muscle activation patterns, and visual performance, so a universal severity-only threshold is difficult to define (553c5528787d2538:p4, p. 22). Linear-only metrics such as the Gadd severity index and head injury criterion are inadequate because rotational acceleration plays an essential role. Forward direction: the injury kernel must take a vector, not a magnitude. The most surprising component is anticipation. Neck muscle strength does not significantly affect injury metrics, whereas early activation of neck muscles, representing awareness of the impact, and proper head posture significantly decrease them (553c5528787d2538:p5, p. 11). The protective variable is timing and belief, not force capacity. A player who perceives the incoming contact pre-activates the neck and braces; a player who is surprised does not, and the same physical hit produces a worse outcome. This is a recursive theory-of-mind structure embedded in tissue: the body's protection depends on its model of the opponent's intent. Retrocausal direction: reconstruct a concussion from its hidden state. The clinical recovery trajectory is not predicted by impact biomechanics (p4, p. 22, refs [67,68,75,81]), so running backward from symptom resolution to a single hit magnitude fails; the genealogy runs through cumulative frequency, location, and the awareness state at each impact, not through one peak g. Cross-layer veto: the awareness channel can veto a physically safe hit classification, a low-magnitude impact to an unbraced, unaware player is not safe, and conversely a high-magnitude hit to a pre-activated, properly postured player may be survivable. The same logic couples to heat: linemen, who train at lower self-generated airspeed, have lower convective and evaporative heat-loss potential and higher exertional-heat-illness risk (p. 18), and their autonomic recovery is already impaired (p6). A high-EV contact call for a lineman in heat is vetoed by the conjunction of thermal strain and incomplete vagal recovery, even when the hit kinematics look acceptable. The isomorphic transfer to the 22-player system is the deception/awareness layer: vulnerability is a vector over exposure, posture, anticipation, and perception, and the simulator must never collapse it to a scalar severity. No football origin is fabricated for the medical invariant; Layer-1 is the source's multidimensional concussion finding, Layer-2 is the explicit mapping onto belief-gated protection and availability.
theory_of_mind: Protection depends on the player's model of the opponent's intent. Early neck activation represents awareness of the impending impact and significantly reduces injury metrics, while neck strength does not (553c5528787d2538:p5, p. 11). The recursive belief clash: a defender who reads the play pre-activates and braces; one who is deceived by a misdirection or comfort call arrives unaware and unbraced, so the same physical contact injures him. The quarterback's internal clock and the defender's tendency read are the same anticipation variable. A high visual performer is less likely to suffer high-severity impacts (p4, ref [77]), confirming that awareness, not toughness, is the protective belief state.
cross_layer_veto: The awareness and thermal layers veto a kinematically safe classification. A low-magnitude hit to an unaware, unbraced player is not safe (553c5528787d2538:p5, p. 11), so the scalar severity gate is overridden by the anticipation gate. For linemen in heat, lower self-generated airspeed reduces convective and evaporative heat loss and raises exertional-heat-illness risk (p. 18), while vagal recovery is already impaired (p6, p. 21). The conjunction of thermal strain and autonomic debt vetoes a high-EV contact call even when head kinematics look acceptable. Physics and physiology jointly overrule the play-call EV.

title: Football: The American Intercollegiate Game
think:
Davis's 1911 monograph is not a playbook but a stratigraphy of rule scars, and reading it as one yields six sovereign primitives that bind the modern 22-player football dynamical system to its legislative history. The author's provenance matters: the title page identifies Parke H. Davis as a member of the Intercollegiate Rules Committee (PDF p12), so the narrative is participant-observation by a legislator, and the appendix reprints the official proceedings he helped write (PDF pp530-577). Where the two disagree, the appendix governs.

The deepest invariant is 55d0f88972ad63be:p3. The 1880 substitution of the scrummage by the scrimmage converted possession from a stochastic contest into a deterministic assignment: the ball is snapped back to a named quarter-back who may not himself rush (Rule 6, PDF p539), and Davis states the consequence explicitly - 'the principle of an orderly retention of the ball by one side, thereby making possible the use of prearranged strategy' (PDF p99). Determinism is the enabling condition of every coordinated-strategy object the Coach-Mind simulator manipulates: without guaranteed retention there is no offense to call plays for, no signal system (PDF p104), no play-call distribution to optimize. But determinism without a progress quota is degenerate, and the book records the degeneracy with unusual precision: in the 1880 Princeton-Yale game Princeton made eleven safeties and Yale six, none of which counted as scoring, and Princeton retained the ball to force a 0-0 draw - the 'block game' (PDF p100). The 1881 sequel forced the safety-counting rule and Princeton's touch-in-goal evasion (PDF pp101-102). The 1882 repair (55d0f88972ad63be:p1, PDF p541) - surrender unless five yards are gained in three consecutive downs - is a reset operator on the possession Markov chain, and its 'consecutive' clause, defined in the same rule as 'without leaving the hands of the side holding it,' marks the exact boundary where the deterministic kernel reverts to contest. Every modern down-and-distance state, third-down conversion rate, and punt decision descends from this operator; the Part II records calibrate it directly ('On the third down, and 3 yards to go,' PDF p222).

The second stratum is valuation (55d0f88972ad63be:p2). The objective function was rewritten four times in twenty years: October 1883 (safety 1, touchdown 2, goal-after 4, field goal 5, PDF p105); December 1883 (touchdown 4, safety 2, goal-after 2, PDF pp105, 542); 1897 (touchdown 5, goal-with-touchdown 6, field goal 5, safety 2, PDF p560); 1904 (field goal reduced to 4, PDF p565). The crossover is decision-theoretic: a bare touchdown is worth less than a field goal until 1897, equal in 1897, and strictly greater only from 1904 - which is why the early game was a kicking game and why fourth-down thresholds cannot be transported across eras. The functional's domain has a hard lower bound: the 1876 code decided matches by majority of touchdowns with a goal equal to four touchdowns (PDF p93), a lexicographic order, not an additive sum; and the Part II records show games played under even stranger local contracts - the 1876 and 1878 Harvard-Yale games counted goals alone by pre-game agreement, and the 1876 game used ten men per side (PDF p300). Any historical simulation that applies one era's weights, or one era's roster size, to another era's games commits exactly the silent-failure error the gatekeeper exists to prevent.

The third stratum is threat (55d0f88972ad63be:p4). The forward pass, legalized in 1906 at the suggestion of John C. Bell and Paul J. Dashiell (PDF p145), produced its chief value 'in the fear of its use by the defensive team, which thereby was compelled to spread and weaken its defence' (PDF p147). This is option value in its purest printed form: any positive pass probability forces coverage allocation even at vanishing pass frequency. The five-yard restriction on the quarter-back run and the forward pass, removed only in the 1910 code (PDF p150), was an exercise in killing option value by constraining the underlying; its removal 'obliterated the checker-board and brought back the famous gridiron' (PDF p150).

The fourth stratum is the regulation cycle (55d0f88972ad63be:p5, PDF p151): V Trick (1884, PDF p108), flying wedge (November 1892, PDF p120), guards-back (PDF p129), tackle-back (1900, PDF p139) - each arises, wins, is charged with injuries and ugliness, is outlawed (the V and flying wedge in 1894, PDF p128), and is replaced by a successor 'still constructed along the lines of the mass idea.' The cycle terminates only when the rule attacks the mechanism rather than the formation: the 1910 code required seven men on the line and forbade hand-or-arm assistance and interlocking (PDF p151). This is the historical proof that instance-bans without mechanism-closure generate successor edges - the same law that governs projection exploitation and market-edge decay.

Finally 55d0f88972ad63be:p6 (PDF p67) is Davis's own epistemic protocol: facts 'obtained from the surviving players,' with the uncertainty of the original occurrence declared rather than smoothed. The book models the gatekeeper's fail-closed doctrine including its failure modes: the Munchener Nachrickten's sensational exaggeration of American football injuries (PDF p125) shows that even participant-adjacent testimony needs adversarial cross-checking, and Camp's injury questionnaire to every former player (PDF p128) is the counter-move - verification by systematic survey. Two editorial defects were quarantined in source_note rather than built upon: the narrative's 'four downs' phrasing (PDF p145) contradicts the three-down rule text and the game records, and the field-goal reduction is dated to the 1903 session in the narrative (PDF p143) but to the March 1904 meeting in the official proceedings (PDF pp564-565). The appendix, not the narrative, is the authoritative stratum - a general lesson for any corpus where commentary and primary text disagree.
theory_of_mind: The sources are saturated with recursive belief, and Davis writes as a legislator who models other minds. The 1906 defense 'feared' a pass that was rarely completed - the defensive coordinator's model of the quarterback's intent, not the quarterback's actual behavior, moved the secondary (PDF p147). After the 1910 code, 'the generals of the gridiron, proceeding cautiously as usual, clung as closely as possible to their old formations, leaving the profound possibilities of the new rules for gradual development' (PDF p154): belief states persist after the payoff structure changes, the same lag a Coach-Mind simulator must model when a coordinator keeps calling mass-era plays because his career was built on them. Camp's injury questionnaire (PDF p128) is a deliberate theory-of-mind instrument - he surveyed every former player to falsify the public's exaggerated injury beliefs with compiled testimony. Davis himself models his readers: he publishes the violations while narrating the reform, calibrating how much scandal the coalition will bear. The quarter-back rule (PDF p539) - the snap receiver may not rush - encodes the committee's belief about which player should hold decision authority, a recursive assignment of who may model whom.
cross_layer_veto: The injury record is the biomechanical veto layer over the tactical-EV layer, and Davis documents the veto firing. Mass plays were high-EV - the tackle-back won Yale victories (PDF p139) - yet the 1909 season's injuries, 'some of these, unfortunately, were fatal,' the first on intercollegiate teams, forced the 1910 removal (PDF pp150-151): expected points cannot outweigh the blunt-trauma and axonal-shear load of interlocked-mass collisions. The flying tackle, 'a spectacular feat, but one frequently provocative of injury,' was forbidden in the same code (PDF p151), and hurdling was placed under referee jurisdiction (PDF p569) - both vetoed by injury mechanics, not by inefficiency. In modern terms, a high-EV quarterback hit or launch-point tackle must be vetoed by the GSI fluid/axonal-shear constraint even when the football-EV layer approves it; the 1910 code is the historical precedent for a cross-layer veto overriding a single-layer optimum. Dexter's injury registry (PDF p142) is the telemetry that made the veto computable: without it the committee argued from anecdote, with it the reform became evidence-driven, and the 1910 mechanism ban could be aimed at the actual injury-producing geometry rather than at its symptoms.

title: ReddiEtAl-2026-MachineLearningSystems-Vol2-AtScale
think: The Reddi volume is not a football book, and that is exactly why it is sovereign for GSE. Every prior layer of the Foundry ontology tells the engine WHAT a snap is: the physics of the trench, the geometry of a coverage shell, the probability calculus of an edge. This volume tells the engine HOW TO RUN the thing that knows all of that. GSE's core deliverable is a 10,000-world snap-by-snap Monte Carlo ensemble adjudicated by JEV, produced by a swarm of extraction and simulation workers. That ensemble is, structurally, a distributed machine-learning fleet. Reddi gives the exact accounting laws of such a fleet, and the isomorphism is not decorative: it is the difference between a crucible that finishes and a crucible that stalls at a barrier while a thousand healthy workers wait on one straggler. Start with the Fleet Law, T_step(N) = T_compute/N + T_comm(N) + T_sync(N) - T_overlap. The naive GSE instinct is that doubling workers halves ensemble time. Reddi shows why that is false: the local compute term halves, but communication and barrier synchronization persist, and the shorter compute window leaves LESS room to hide transfers, so T_overlap shrinks too. The step on 2N devices takes well over half as long. This is the single most important operational fact for the Foundry: adding workers to a communication-bound ontology workload can make the crucible SLOWER. The diagnostic is f_compute = (T_compute/N)/T_step; below 0.5, more than half the step lies outside useful local arithmetic, and the C3 taxonomy tells you whether the binding axis is Compute (the snap physics), Communication (ontology-state transfer), or Coordination (straggler waiting, recovery, JEV adjudication barriers). The scaling law supplies the budget logic. L(X) = A_L X^{-alpha_scale} + C_L says estimation error decays as a power law toward an irreducible floor. For GSE, X is world-count and C_L is the aleatoric noise floor of football itself: the uncertainty no simulation removes, the same noise term Prince separates from bias and variance. The exponent is the price list: halving Monte Carlo error costs 2^{1/alpha_scale} more worlds. And Chinchilla's compute-optimal result is a direct warning against GSE's natural failure mode: over-building the ontology (parameters) while simulating too few worlds (tokens). GPT-3 was undertrained at 1.7 tokens/parameter against Chinchilla's ~20; a GSE ontology of enormous depth validated on a handful of worlds is the same mistake. The IsoFLOP valley, not maximal ontology sophistication, is the target. The 6PD law (O_train ~ 6PD) is the work-accounting bridge: it converts a budget into FLOPs, and FLOPs must never be confused with FLOP/s, because time = work/(eta_hw R_peak). Then the reliability arithmetic turns failure from an exception into a steady state. A_all = A_component^N and MTBF_system = MTTF_component/N mean that a swarm of N workers, each individually dependable, fails routinely as a whole. The Llama-3 measurement (419 interruptions in 54 days on 16,384 GPUs, MTTF ~3.1h) is the empirical anchor. For the Foundry this is not a hypothetical: a long extraction run accumulates dozens of expected worker failures, so the gatekeeper must checkpoint and recover as normal execution. Young-Daly gives the cadence: T*_ckpt = sqrt(2 T_write MTBF_system), using SYSTEM MTBF, not per-worker lifetime (which overestimates by sqrt(N)). And because MTBF collapses as 1/N, the lever is MTTR: A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) shows cutting recovery 30min->5min raises availability 90.91%->98.36%. Engineer recovery, not component perfection. The memory and communication layers close the loop. The Roofline, min(R_peak, BW x I), and the precision-dependent ridge point I_ridge = R_peak/BW tell GSE whether a snap kernel is ontology-lookup-bound (low arithmetic intensity, memory-bound) or physics-bound (high intensity, compute-bound), and that batching worlds over a shared coverage shell is how you raise intensity above the ridge. The alpha-beta model T(n)=alpha+n/beta with crossover n*=alpha*beta prices every swarm message and tells you to fuse small snap-state updates (latency-bound) but compress large ontology tensors (bandwidth-bound). Ring AllReduce keeps per-worker aggregation volume ~constant as the swarm grows, where a central aggregator saturates. The 3D cube N=N_DP x N_PP x N_TP is the GSE partition: worlds x snap-stages x ontology-shards, each axis mapped to the interconnect tier that can carry its traffic. And the data-parallel invariant is a correctness gate: the ensemble must weight each world by its valid sample count, because an unweighted mean of unequal worlds overweights the sparse ones and silently corrupts the edge posterior. The three scaling phases map cleanly onto GSE's lifecycle and decide which part of the fleet carries the load. Pretraining scaling is the one long, failure-sensitive foundation run: building and calibrating the ontology corpus, where scaling-law gains must be realized in wall-clock time and checkpoint cadence is survival. Posttraining scaling replaces that single job with many smaller, coordination-heavy runs: GSE's per-week calibration and RLVR veto tuning, where the bottleneck shifts from raw throughput to orchestration. Test-time scaling spends compute on each request: GSE's per-game crucible, where additional worlds trade serving latency for a possible quality gain and compete with the pick-publication deadline. Reddi is explicit that the schematic curves establish no universal efficiency ranking, so GSE must compare measured task improvement against cost before choosing where to spend the next increment of compute. The energy account closes the budget: rho_energy = O_useful/(E_device+E_cooling+E_network) in FLOP/J, and communication energy is bytes sent times the energy per bit of every boundary crossed (a fabric-path midpoint ~35 pJ/bit gives ~5.6 kJ per 1GB reduction, paid again every synchronous step). An algorithm that moves fewer bytes, or a placement that keeps them inside the node, saves energy as directly as it saves time. For a zero-cost-bound Foundry this is not an afterthought: the swarm's electricity and egress are part of the honest cost of a crucible, and the same Amdahl accounting that bounds a partial speedup bounds every partial energy saving. The deepest point is the Byzantine/SDC taxonomy. A worker that returns wrong snap values while passing every liveness check is the fleet analogue of a corrupted world simulation poisoning the ensemble. Checksums of wrong bytes still pass; only independent recomputation, invariants, or model-level evidence expose it. That is precisely the gatekeeper's mandate: verify completion, do not assume it. Reddi thus supplies the operational constitution of the Foundry swarm, and every equation is a load-bearing wall, not a metaphor.
theory_of_mind: Recursive theory of mind: the fleet engineer models the straggler, who is itself a worker modeling its own local queue; the scheduler models the engineer's recovery policy; the adversary models the fleet's validation. GSE mirrors this recursion exactly: the offense models the defense's coverage shell, the defense models the offense's tendency, and the GSE engine models BOTH models while JEV adjudicates. Reddi's C3 lens is a theory of mind about the machine: an idle accelerator does not identify its own bottleneck, so the operator must infer whether it waits on operands, a transfer, or a failed peer. title: 578457115b76903d
think: Begin from the invariant the paper actually proves rather than the headline gain. The season operator S(R) integrates an optimal-lineup kernel L(R,w) over the remaining week index, and the playoff reweighting introduces a second measure on that same index. The crucial structural fact is the conservation identity alpha_p*n_p + alpha_n*n_n = n_p + n_n, which forces g_a^w = g_a whenever per-week gains are constant. Read as a change of measure, the Radon-Nikodym derivative is alpha_p on playoff weeks and alpha_n elsewhere, normalized so total mass is preserved under a flat gain profile. This is why the bias is described as subtle: an opponent who audits only the unweighted total sees no distortion, because the distortion lives entirely in the covariance between the weight field and the per-week gain field. If gains are flat, the covariance is zero and the deception is invisible even in principle; the advantage materializes only when the acquired assets have asymmetric late-season schedules. Now bind this to the 22-player dynamical system. The same conservation structure governs end-game leverage management: a coordinator does not create expected points out of nothing, but redistributes a fixed season-long expectation toward the possessions where win probability is most sensitive, namely fourth-quarter and playoff drives. The week index in the fantasy kernel is isomorphic to the possession-leverage index in the game kernel; alpha_p is the leverage multiplier; n_n is the stock of low-leverage possessions from which mass is borrowed. The singularity at n_n = 0 is the moment there are no low-leverage possessions left to borrow from, which is exactly the two-minute / playoff regime where every snap is high-leverage and the reweighting denominator vanishes. The projection tables make the hidden state concrete. Kimani Vidal's projection collapses from roughly 14 points in weeks 8-11 to roughly 2.5-3.0 in weeks 13-17 (p.17), a regime break baked into the ESPN field that the GA reads as a tradable asset depreciation. Drake Maye carries a week-14 zero (bye, p.15) and strong weeks 15-17, which is precisely the late-season asymmetry the playoff weight is designed to harvest. Brandon Aiyuk is zero through week 14 then reappears near 8 points (p.14), an injury-return discontinuity. These are not noise; they are the non-stationary structure that makes the covariance term nonzero and the deception profitable. Finally, the cross-layer caution: S(R) and g_a^w are point estimates with no variance term, and the paper itself flags injury, coaching, and weather divergence (p.7). A gain computed on a collapsing projection is a tail-risk trap, so the mathematically optimal reweighting can be vetoed by the physical uncertainty it ignores. The invariant survives; the decision built on it must be gated by realized-versus-projected telemetry before execution.
theory_of_mind: Three belief states clash under pressure. The initiator (team A) believes playoff weeks decide championships and weights them 1.2-1.5x. The partner (team B) evaluates on unweighted overall projections and, the paper assumes, does not scrutinize playoff weeks (p.3). The commissioner models both for collusion and can veto (p.7). Recursively, A models B's unweighted audit, B may suspect A's intent, and the commissioner watches the pair. This is the coach comfort call (the apparently fair trade B accepts) versus the DC tendency trap (A's hidden playoff tilt) versus the QB internal clock (the seeding deadline that forces the decision).
cross_layer_veto: The high-EV low-beta trade (22.44 versus 10.82) is vetoed by two lower layers. Psychology vetoes execution: the asymmetry triggers rejection or a collusion veto, so the nominally optimal deal never lands. Physics vetoes the estimate: the gain rests on ESPN projections that diverge via injury, coaching, and weather (p.7), and on a collapsing asset (Vidal's weeks 13-17 drop to ~2.5, p.17) with no variance term. The structural g_b>0 constraint is itself a veto on pure extraction. High EV on a point estimate is therefore not actionable EV.

title: 578457115b76903d
think: The second invariant is the acceptance kernel hidden inside the cost function. The term gamma*|g_a^w - g_b| penalizes disparity, but it measures disparity between the weighted user gain and the unweighted partner gain. That asymmetry is the deception: the user optimizes a playoff-tilted objective while the fairness channel displays an unweighted comparison the partner is expected to perform. The win-win constraints g_a>0 and g_b>0 are the structural guarantee that the counterparty still perceives benefit, which is what makes the proposal executable at all. In effect the cost function encodes a theory of mind of the partner: most partners evaluate overall projections without scrutinizing playoff weeks (p.3), so the apparent-fairness channel is calibrated to that specific belief. Map this onto the 22-player system as a deception-acceptance kernel. A play-action fake only pays off if the defense accepts the run read; the hidden advantage (the pass behind the linebackers) is gated by the counterparty's belief state. The fairness penalty is the analogue of making the fake look structurally sound enough to be accepted, while the playoff weight is the hidden advantage that only resolves after acceptance. The commissioner veto and collusion concerns (p.7) are the league-level theory of mind that can reject a proposal even when both managers accept, adding a third recursive layer: the user models the partner, the partner may model the user's intent, and the commissioner models both. The evolutionary machinery is the search over this acceptance-constrained space. Hybrid elitism keeps the top fifteen overall plus the top two per partner, which is diversity preservation against premature convergence onto a single opponent, isomorphic to keeping multiple disguised coverages alive so the offense cannot key on one tendency. The six mutation operators, with keep-same at 0.2 and the rest at 0.16, balance local refinement (exchange, add/remove) against broad exploration (spawn-new with a random opponent B'). The probabilistic 0.3 retention of higher-cost trades is an explicit exploration temperature that prevents the population from collapsing into a single basin. The empirical lever law closes the loop. High alpha=1.2 maximizes user gain (average 13.62) but concedes more to the opponent (20.69 on the top trade); low beta=0.8 extracts the most asymmetric deal (22.44 versus 10.82) by exploiting roster imbalance; high gamma=0.4 produces the most negotiable balanced deal (20.01 versus 18.94). These are aggressiveness dials, isomorphic to go-for-it versus punt: own expected value weighed against concession. The cross-layer veto is decisive here. The low-beta 22.44-point gain is nominally highest EV, but it is vetoed twice: by psychology, because the asymmetry triggers rejection or a collusion veto so the trade never executes, and by physics, because the gain rests on projections that can collapse (Vidal's late-season drop) and on a single-league snapshot with no variance model. The win-win constraint g_b>0 is itself a built-in veto on pure extraction. The lesson for the Coach-Mind sim and for DFS portfolio construction is identical: a point-estimate optimum that ignores acceptance feasibility and tail variance is not an optimum at all, and no sportsbook odds are needed or used to see this.
theory_of_mind: The cost function is a frozen theory of mind of the partner: gamma*|g_a^w - g_b| is tuned to a counterparty who compares unweighted totals, while the user secretly optimizes the weighted g_a^w. Under pressure the partner may recompute weighted gains and detect the tilt, the commissioner may read collusion, and the user must anticipate both. This mirrors the coach's comfort call versus the DC's tendency trap versus the QB's internal clock: the visible fairness is the comfort call that gets accepted, the playoff tilt is the trap that resolves only after acceptance, and the seeding clock forces the timing.
cross_layer_veto: The fairness-emphasis deal (20.01 versus 18.94, gamma=0.4) is the negotiable optimum, yet even it is vetoed when projection uncertainty dominates: a balanced point estimate built on diverging ESPN inputs (p.7) carries tail risk the objective cannot see. Psychology vetoes the asymmetric low-beta alternative outright through rejection and veto risk. The cross-layer rule is that execution feasibility (a psychological acceptance channel) and realized-versus-projected variance (a physical channel) both override the raw cost minimum, so the GA's lowest-cost trade is not automatically the decision.

title: 1318-formation-impact-double-machine-learning
think: The transition from standard Double Machine Learning (DML) to Heterogeneous DML represents a fundamental shift from estimating a scalar Average Treatment Effect (ATE) to resolving a high-dimensional Conditional Average Treatment Effect (CATE) surface. Standard DML relies on Neyman orthogonality to neutralize the first-order bias introduced by slow-converging nuisance parameter estimators (e.g., propensity scores and outcome regressions). However, as highlighted in the text, an ATE often masks critical strategic nuances—specifically, that certain tactical decisions (like fourth-down attempts) yield vastly different returns depending on the precise game state (trailing late, specific field positions). To extract this, we project the residualized treatment and outcome onto a causal forest. This tree-based partitioning effectively performs a localized DML estimation within each leaf node. The mathematical rigor demands that these localized estimates remain robust; hence, the necessity of the 'nuisance learner stability' check. If XGBoost and Random Forest yield divergent signs on significant effects, the orthogonality condition is likely violated by high-frequency noise or overfitting in the nuisance stages. Furthermore, the 'placebo refutation veto' acts as a strict epistemic gatekeeper. In sports analytics, spurious correlations abound due to complex, adaptive opposing strategies. A causal claim that survives a placebo test—where a fake treatment applied to the same rich feature set yields zero effect—possesses a much higher degree of sovereignty. This multi-layered validation ensures that the resulting CATE surface is not merely an artifact of model flexibility but a genuine representation of underlying causal mechanics, ready for deployment in real-time decision support systems.
theory_of_mind: Modeling the opposing coach requires acknowledging they are not a static distribution but an adaptive agent actively trying to exploit our tendencies. When we estimate the CATE of a 'go-decision', we implicitly model the opponent's defensive reaction function embedded within the outcome variable. If the opponent anticipates our aggression when trailing late, the observed effect might be dampened. The heterogeneous DML approach, by slicing the data into granular game states, attempts to isolate moments where our action precedes their adaptation, capturing the true causal leverage before the opponent's theory of mind updates their defensive scheme.
cross_layer_veto: A critical cross-layer veto must be applied to prevent leakage from the future game state into the current treatment assignment. For instance, if 'score differential' is used as a covariate in the causal forest, we must ensure we are not inadvertently using post-treatment variables that are themselves outcomes of the decision. Additionally, anti-collinearity checks are vital; if the nuisance learners (XGBoost/RF) are too similar in their architectural biases, they might co-fail on specific edge cases (e.g., garbage time plays), producing a false sense of stability. The placebo test serves as the ultimate veto against such hidden collinearities or data leakage, ensuring the estimated causal surface is genuinely exogenous.

While TPE is an efficient global optimization algorithm for black-box functions, its application here merely minimizes cross-sectional Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) at a frozen timestamp $t_0$. For GSE, our primitive requirement is a state-space model capable of generating probability mass functions over future states $S_{t+k}$ given current observations $O_t$. A deterministic point estimate of a player's market value possesses zero entropy regarding their future on-pitch performance or injury likelihood. title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
primitive_name: Statistical learning framework (learner blind to D)
gse_mapping: GSE's pre-game model is trained on a finite sample of historical games S drawn from the unknown distribution D of football situations, blind to the true outcome-generating process. The PAC framework is the correct model for the PRE-GAME calibration target (an i.i.d. outcome distribution), exactly as the online framework is correct for the in-game adversarial sequence.
verbatim_quote: It is important to note that we do not assume that the learner knows anything about this distribution.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE must not memorize historical outcomes. A model that perfectly retrodicts every past game (L_S=0) but fails on new games is the papaya memorizer — exactly the overfitting failure. GSE's calibration discipline (hold-out validation, restricted model class) is the ERM-with-inductive-bias cure.
verbatim_quote: Although the ERM rule seems very natural, without being careful, this approach may fail miserably.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
primitive_name: Inductive bias (hypothesis class as prior knowledge)
gse_mapping: The GSE football ontology (formations, coverage shells, down-distance tendencies, personnel groupings) IS the inductive bias H, fixed before seeing the game data. No-free-lunch (below) says this prior knowledge is mandatory: there is no universal football learner. The ontology is not decoration, it is the restriction that makes generalization possible.
verbatim_quote: Since the choice of such a restriction is determined before the learner sees the training data, it should ideally be based on some prior knowledge about the problem to be learned.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's pre-game model carries a PAC guarantee: trained on m historical games, with confidence 1-delta its true calibration error is within epsilon of the best in-class model. The sample-complexity law m >= log(|H|/delta)/epsilon tells GSE how many historical games it needs for a given calibration accuracy and confidence — a concrete data-budget rule.
verbatim_quote: The definition of Probably Approximately Correct learnability contains two approximation parameters.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
primitive_name: Agnostic PAC and the Bayes optimal predictor
gse_mapping: Football is agnostic, not realizable: the same situation produces different outcomes (stochastic labels). GSE cannot reach zero error or the Bayes optimum; its honest target is to be within epsilon of the best model in its ontology class. The Bayes predictor is the irreducible-calibration floor GSE competes against, never claims to beat.
verbatim_quote: Clearly, we cannot hope that the learning algorithm will find a hypothesis whose error is smaller than the minimal possible error, that of the Bayes predictor.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's historical calibration must hold UNIFORMLY over its whole model class, not just for the model it happened to pick. If GSE selects the best-fitting model on historical data, the guarantee that its hold-out calibration is close requires uniform convergence over the ontology class — otherwise it is cherry-picking a model that overfits the sample.
verbatim_quote: Put another way, we need that uniformly over all hypotheses in the hypothesis class, the empirical risk will be close to the true risk

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's finite shell-library calibration gets a concrete finite-sample rate from Hoeffding + union bound: m >= log(2|H|/delta)/(2 eps^2) historical games guarantee uniform eps-calibration with confidence 1-delta. Derived kernel: GSE computes its calibration data budget from this bound, and uses the discretization trick only as a rough sanity estimate, not a rigorous guarantee.
verbatim_quote: Instead, we will use a measure concentration inequality due to Hoeffding, which quantifies the gap between empirical averages and their expected value.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: No-Free-Lunch is the formal justification that GSE MUST encode football-specific prior knowledge (the ontology). There is no universal sports predictor; a generic learner fails on football while a football-biased learner succeeds. The '99% AI Whale' tout with a domain-free model is exactly the universal learner the theorem condemns. GSE's edge comes from its inductive bias, not from a magic universal algorithm.
verbatim_quote: the theorem states that for binary classification prediction tasks, for every learner there exists a distribution on which it fails.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's ontology richness is a bias-complexity dial: a richer football ontology (more coverages, more situational splits) lowers approximation error (better fit to reality) but raises estimation error (overfitting the historical sample). GSE must tune ontology complexity to the available data budget — the central model-design tradeoff, made quantitative.
verbatim_quote: The first component reflects the quality of our prior knowledge, measured by the minimal risk of a hypothesis in our hypothesis class

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
primitive_name: Approximation error vanishes only under realizability
gse_mapping: GSE diagnoses whether its calibration error is a bias floor (approximation error, ontology too poor) or an overfitting gap (estimation error, ontology too rich for the data). Derived kernel: if hold-out error plateaus as data grows, the bottleneck is approximation error and GSE must enrich the ontology, not collect more games.
verbatim_quote: Under the realizability assumption, the approximation error is zero.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
primitive_name: Shattering and the VC epistemic motto
gse_mapping: This is GSE's epistemic motto in one line: a model that can fit every possible outcome has zero predictive power. If GSE's ontology can realize every labeling of a set of situations (shatters it), it explains everything and predicts nothing. GSE must bound the VCdim of its read classes — a coverage model that 'always has an explanation' for any result is the worthless explainer the theorem condemns.
verbatim_quote: If someone can explain every phenomenon, his explanations are worthless.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's model class is learnable iff its VCdim is finite, and its sample complexity is Theta((d+log(1/delta))/eps^2). This is the master law connecting GSE's ontology complexity (d), data budget (m), calibration accuracy (eps), and confidence (delta). GSE reads its required historical-game count directly off the VCdim of its read class.
verbatim_quote: Not only does the VC-dimension characterize PAC learnability; it even determines the sample complexity.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's infinite ontology class (continuous parameters) is still learnable because its effective size on m situations grows only polynomially (em/d)^d once m exceeds VCdim. Derived kernel: GSE uses the growth-function bound to convert its combinatorial ontology complexity into a concrete uniform-convergence/sample-complexity guarantee, rather than treating the class as infinitely large.
verbatim_quote: when m becomes larger than the VC-dimension, the growth function increases polynomially rather than exponentially with m.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
primitive_name: VC dimension is not parameter count
gse_mapping: GSE must not estimate model complexity by counting ontology features/parameters. A single finely-tuned continuous parameter (like a threshold sweep) can have infinite VCdim and be unlearnable. Derived kernel: GSE measures the combinatorial capacity (VCdim/growth) of its read classes directly, because feature count is an unreliable complexity proxy.
verbatim_quote: While this is often the case, it is not always true.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's pre-game fit is Regularized Loss Minimization: minimize historical calibration loss plus a complexity penalty lambda‖w‖^2 on the read-weights. The regularizer is the stabilizer that keeps one anomalous historical game from swinging the whole model — the batch analogue of the online FTRL regularizer. Ridge gives GSE a closed-form, well-conditioned pre-game estimator.
verbatim_quote: Another view of regularization is as a stabilizer of the learning algorithm.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
primitive_name: Replace-one stability equals the generalization gap
gse_mapping: GSE gets a concrete, measurable generalization diagnostic: its pre-game generalization gap EQUALS how much its prediction changes when one historical game is swapped out (replace-one stability). GSE can estimate this directly by leave-one-out perturbation. The oracle inequality bounds GSE's risk by best-in-class + regularization + stability, and tunes lambda to balance them.
verbatim_quote: Intuitively, a learning algorithm is stable if a small change of the input to the algorithm does not change the output of the algorithm much.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
gse_mapping: GSE trains its pre-game model by SGD: each iteration samples ONE fresh historical game and steps along its (unbiased) loss subgradient, w^{t+1}=w^t−eta v_t. This is how GSE scales to large historical corpora without full-batch passes. The B rho/sqrt(T) rate sets GSE's training-iteration budget, and strong convexity (from the Tikhonov regularizer) accelerates it to log(T)/T.
verbatim_quote: In stochastic gradient descent we do not require the update direction to be based exactly on the gradient.

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
primitive_name: SGD minimizes true risk from a single fresh example
gse_mapping: GSE's SGD targets the TRUE pre-game calibration risk directly, one fresh historical game at a time, rather than minimizing the empirical historical error — which is precisely why it generalizes instead of memorizing. The single-fresh-example unbiased gradient is the batch counterpart of the online bandit's single-outcome feedback. Online-to-batch (Shalev-Shwartz 2012) and this PAC/SGD theory are the two halves of GSE's learning pipeline.
verbatim_quote: With SGD, however, all we need is to find an unbiased estimate of the gradient

title: ShalevShwartzBenDavid-2014-UnderstandingMachineLearning
think: If the 2012 online-learning monograph gave GSE its in-game constitution, this 2014 textbook gives it its pre-game epistemology. The two are complementary halves of one pipeline: online learning governs the adversarial snap-by-snap sequence inside a game, and statistical learning theory governs how the pre-game model generalizes from a finite sample of historical games. The book opens with the decisive admission that the learner knows nothing about the data-generating distribution D. GSE's pre-game model is exactly this blind learner: it sees a finite sample S of historical situations drawn i.i.d. from the unknown distribution of football, and must output a predictor whose true error is small. The i.i.d. assumption is appropriate HERE, at the pre-game boundary, even though it fails inside the game — and online-to-batch is the theorem that lets the in-game online learner be converted into this batch setting. The first danger is overfitting. Empirical Risk Minimization, the natural rule of fitting the training data as well as possible, can fail miserably: the memorizing predictor has zero training error and one-half true error. A GSE model that perfectly retrodicts every past game but cannot predict a new one is this memorizer. The cure is not to abandon ERM but to restrict it to a hypothesis class H chosen before seeing the data — the inductive bias. For GSE that class IS the football ontology: formations, coverage shells, down-distance tendencies, personnel logic. The No-Free-Lunch theorem makes this mandatory rather than optional: for every learner there is a distribution on which it fails, so there is no universal football predictor. The domain-free 'AI Whale' tout is precisely the universal learner the theorem condemns; GSE's edge comes from its football-specific prior knowledge, not from a magic algorithm. PAC learnability quantifies the guarantee: with m >= log(|H|/delta)/epsilon historical games, the ERM model is, with confidence 1-delta, within epsilon of correct. Because football is agnostic — the same situation yields different outcomes — GSE cannot reach the Bayes optimum or zero error; its honest target is to be within epsilon of the best model in its ontology class. The engine of the guarantee is uniform convergence: the empirical risk must approximate the true risk uniformly over the WHOLE class, not just for the model GSE happened to pick, otherwise selection cherry-picks an overfit. Hoeffding's concentration inequality plus a union bound gives the finite-class rate m_UC <= log(2|H|/delta)/(2 epsilon^2), a concrete finite-sample calibration budget. The bias-complexity tradeoff then decomposes GSE's error into approximation error (the quality of the ontology, min over H of the true risk, independent of sample size) and estimation error (the overfitting gap, growing with class complexity). A richer ontology lowers bias but raises overfitting risk; if hold-out error plateaus as data grows, the bottleneck is the approximation floor and GSE must enrich the ontology rather than collect more games. The combinatorial heart is the VC dimension. A class shatters a set if it realizes every possible labeling of it, and the book's motto is the epistemic core of the whole Foundry: if someone can explain every phenomenon, his explanations are worthless. A coverage model that always has an explanation for any result predicts nothing. The fundamental theorem unifies six conditions — uniform convergence, ERM, PAC and agnostic PAC learnability, and finite VC dimension — into one object, and pins the sample complexity at Theta((d+log(1/delta))/epsilon^2). Crucially, VC dimension is NOT parameter count: a single oscillating parameter ceil(0.5 sin(theta x)) has infinite VC dimension, so GSE must measure combinatorial capacity directly, never count ontology features. Sauer's lemma is what rescues infinite classes: once the sample exceeds the VC dimension the growth function turns from exponential to polynomial, (em/d)^d, so a continuous ontology is still learnable. The optimization layer closes the loop. Regularized Loss Minimization adds a Tikhonov penalty lambda‖w‖^2 to the empirical risk; ridge regression gives a closed-form, well-conditioned pre-game estimator. The deep result is that stability EQUALS generalization: the expected true-minus-empirical error is exactly the on-average-replace-one stability, how much the prediction swings when a single historical game is swapped out. GSE can measure this directly by leave-one-out perturbation, and the oracle inequality bounds its risk by best-in-class plus lambda‖w*‖^2 plus 2rho^2/(lambda m), tuning lambda to balance fit against stability. Finally SGD minimizes the TRUE risk directly from a single fresh example per iteration, because the single-example gradient is an unbiased estimate of the risk gradient; it generalizes without memorizing precisely because it never targets the empirical sample. The convex-Lipschitz rate B rho/sqrt(T) sets the training budget, and the Tikhonov-induced strong convexity accelerates it to log(T)/T. Two further distinctions keep the pipeline honest. The book separates the STATISTICAL aspect of learning (how many examples suffice) from the COMPUTATIONAL aspect (how much runtime the learner needs); Valiant's original PAC definition demands both be polynomial, and GSE must respect both — a statistically learnable class is useless if fitting it exceeds the crucible's compute budget, which is where the fleet layer's laws re-enter. And model selection must run on a held-out validation set, never the training set: GSE tunes the regularization strength lambda and the ontology complexity on validation, because selecting on training data overfits the selection itself and silently inflates the claimed calibration. Every equation is a load-bearing law of GSE's pre-game generalization, the batch half of the pipeline whose online half was laid down by the 2012 monograph.
theory_of_mind: Recursive theory of mind: the No-Free-Lunch and VC proofs are adversarial theory-of-mind constructions. The adversary chooses the distribution D AFTER seeing the learner A, concentrates it on a shattered set, and picks a target labeling that contradicts A on the unobserved half — it reasons about what the learner can and cannot infer from its sample. GSE mirrors this: the defense reasons about the offense's tendencies, and the engine must reason about what an adversary could force it to mispredict. The replace-one stability diagnostic is itself a theory-of-mind probe: how much does the model's belief change when one piece of evidence is swapped, i.e. how sensitive is its reasoning to a single observation. A model that swings wildly on one swapped game is reasoning fragilely, exactly as an unstable online learner oscillates.
cross_layer_veto: Cross-layer veto adjudication: the online layer (2012) VETOES applying i.i.d. PAC guarantees to the in-game adversarial sequence — those belong only at the pre-game batch boundary, reached via online-to-batch. The VC layer VETOES any read class with infinite VC dimension as unlearnable, and VETOES parameter-count complexity claims (the sin counterexample). The bias-complexity layer VETOES enriching the ontology beyond the data budget (estimation error) and VETOES collecting more data to fix an approximation floor. think: The Foundry's stack now has its neurons (Nielsen), representations (Prince), fleet (Reddi), in-game online constitution (Shalev-Shwartz 2012), pre-game generalization epistemology (Shalev-Shwartz & Ben-David 2014), and play-call decision theory (Szepesvari). Zhang, Lipton, Li and Smola's textbook supplies the algorithms layer: the actual neural machinery that implements all of it. This is where the abstract laws become runnable components. The centerpiece is attention. The intuition is that rather than compressing the whole input into one fixed vector — the seq2seq bottleneck that fails on long sequences — the decoder should revisit the input at every step and selectively focus on what matters. For GSE this is the formation/coverage reader: the query is the current game state, the keys and values are the playbook and coverage library, and attention pooling aggregates them into a contextual read. The weights are a convex combination — nonnegative, summing to one — produced by softmax, which is the SAME simplex link function as the online layer's entropic mirror descent and the RL layer's Boltzmann policy. Softmax is the universal differentiable map from scores to a calibrated distribution, and its gradient never vanishes. The scaled dot-product scoring function q^T k/sqrt(d) is a numerical-stability necessity: for d-dimensional unit-variance keys the dot product has variance d, and without the 1/sqrt(d) rescaling the softmax saturates into a hard argmax with vanishing gradients. GSE must scale its situation-shell logits by 1/sqrt(d) or its coverage selection collapses. Additive attention bridges mismatched query/key feature spaces via a learned tanh MLP. Multi-head attention runs several such poolings in parallel over different learned representation subspaces, so the engine can simultaneously attend to coverage, personnel, and down-distance cues rather than committing to a single similarity notion. Self-attention lets every element of the game state attend to every other, building the contextual representation where a coverage shell's meaning depends on the whole formation; it has O(1) path length (easy long-range dependencies) and O(1) sequential operations (fully parallel) but O(n^2 d) compute — the fleet layer's budget caps how large a state the engine can read. Because self-attention is order-blind, positional encoding restores the drive's play order, and its rotation property lets the engine reason about relative snap offsets. The Transformer stacks multi-head self-attention and positionwise feed-forward sublayers with residual connections and layer normalization, and masked decoder attention preserves the autoregressive property — GSE's prediction for snap i may depend only on snaps already played, never on the future, the architectural twin of the online layer's round-by-round causality. The output head is softmax plus cross-entropy, and its gradient is the most important single equation in the book for GSE: softmax(o)_j − y_j, the predicted probability minus the revealed reality. This is the calibration-surprise signal, and it is the SAME object as the RL layer's TD error and the online layer's loss subgradient — the universal prediction-minus-reality update that drives all three learning layers, a consequence of the exponential-family structure of the log-likelihood. The cross-entropy loss itself is bounded below by zero and incurs INFINITE loss for a confident wrong prediction (−log 0 = infinity). This is the loss-level death of the tout's lock: a model that assigns probability zero to an outcome that occurs is infinitely penalized, so GSE must keep every possible outcome nonzero — the loss-level twin of the online layer's Cover convexification. The training dynamics are the optimization chapter. SGD samples one example and steps along its unbiased gradient at O(1) cost instead of O(n), the same single-fresh-example mechanism as the PAC layer's SGD-for-risk and the RL layer's Q-learning. A constant learning rate never settles (persistent noise), so the rate must decay dynamically — polynomial inverse-sqrt (alpha=0.5) is the convex-safe choice, the same 1/sqrt(t) law as the online layer's eta and the RL layer's Robbins-Monro conditions. Momentum replaces the instantaneous gradient with a velocity, a leaky average of past gradients (the heavy ball), aggregating aligned gradients in flat directions and cancelling oscillations in steep ones — the cure for the ill-conditioned canyon of a high-dimensional ontology loss landscape. Adam combines SGD, minibatching, momentum, and per-coordinate preconditioning with bias-corrected EWMA moments (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-6), and is GSE's training workhorse. But Adam is NOT universally convergent: Reddi et al. proved it can diverge in convex settings when the second moment blows up, and Yogi's sign-controlled update fixes it. GSE must monitor the second moment and fall back to Yogi or larger minibatches — the fail-closed discipline applied to the optimizer itself. Finally regularization. Weight decay adds (lambda/2)‖w‖^2, restricting parameter size, the deep-learning twin of the PAC layer's Tikhonov stabilizer; lambda is tuned on validation, and because plain Adam conflates weight decay with ℓ2 regularization GSE uses decoupled AdamW. Dropout zeros activations with probability p and rescales survivors by 1/(1−p) (unbiased), breaking co-adaptation; Bishop's theorem that input-noise training equals Tikhonov regularization ties it to the same stability principle, and test-time dropout gives GSE an uncertainty estimate — agreement across dropout samples is the engine's confidence signal. Every equation is a load-bearing component of GSE's neural engine: the attention reader, the calibrated softmax head, the prediction-minus-reality gradient, the SGD/momentum/Adam training dynamics, and the weight-decay/dropout regularization that bounds generalization. The algorithms layer is where the Foundry's abstract laws become a runnable, calibrated, fail-closed predictor.
theory_of_mind: Recursive theory of mind: attention is a differentiable theory-of-mind mechanism — the query models what the decoder needs to know, the keys model what each input token offers, and the softmax weights are the decoder's belief about which tokens are relevant to its current prediction. In GSE the recursion is literal: the engine's query (the current situation) attends over the coverage library (the defense's possible responses), weighting each shell by its compatibility — a model of the defense's mind. Self-attention extends this to every element modeling every other, the formation reading itself. The cross-entropy gradient (prediction minus reality) is the engine correcting its model of the world against what actually happened, the same surprise-driven belief update as the online and RL layers.
cross_layer_veto: Cross-layer veto adjudication: the fleet layer (Reddi) VETOES self-attention states whose O(n^2 d) cost exceeds the crucible budget. The numerical layer VETOES unscaled dot-product logits (softmax saturation, vanishing gradients) — the 1/sqrt(d) scaling is mandatory. The online layer (Cover) and the loss layer VETO any zero-probability outcome (infinite cross-entropy penalty for a confident wrong lock). The causality layer VETOES unmasked decoder attention (future-snap leakage). The optimizer layer VETOES treating Adam as universally convergent (Reddi divergence) and demands a Yogi/larger-batch fallback under high gradient variance. The PAC layer VETOES tuning weight decay on training data (must be validation) and VETOES conflating Adam weight decay with ℓ2 regularization (use AdamW). When layers conflict the binding constraint wins and the gatekeeper PASSes rather than fabricating a guarantee: a diverging optimizer or a saturated attention head is refused, not published. title: 5c31b5de385d42ac
primitive_name: PFR uncertainty kernel: square-root time decay of outcome variance with empirical 13.45-point anchor
gse_mapping: The sqrt(t/T) variance contraction is isomorphic to a diffusion bridge pinned at a terminal horizon: remaining-time uncertainty shrinks as the square root of the remaining interval. In GSE it becomes the posterior-SD schedule on game outcome, calibrated per time bucket against empirical residual margins instead of a single global constant; in GSI the same horizon-shrinking filter pattern applies to clinical telemetry trend alarms approaching an event horizon (isomorphism only - the source makes no physiological claim).
verbatim_quote: SDPFR = uncertainty ´ sqrt(min.rem / 60), where pts.off is the number of points scored by the team on offense, pts.def is the number of points scored by the team on defense, exp.pts is the expected points for the current drive, line is the Vegas line at kickoff (coded here as the amount by which the team on offense is favored to win, negative if they were favored to lose), min.rem is the time remaining in the game expressed as minutes (e.g., 60 min at kickoff, 7.5 min midway through the 4th quarter, 0 min at the end of regulation play), and uncertainty is the standard deviation of the difference between actual game outcomes (score differential) and Vegas lines (i.e., final game pts.off minus pts.def minus line). PFR uses uncertainty = 13.45 based on their analysis of historical game outcomes.

The kernel is closed-form (normal CDF), spreadsheet-cheap (p8), and fits the Coach-Mimic persona layer that must explain decisions to non-statistical coaches (p17).
verbatim_quote: Win probability is calculated as the area under the curve above a threshold of 0.5 (which represents favorable game outcomes for the team on offense, or the probability that they will win) plus one-half the area between thresholds of -0.5 and 0.5 (which represents a tied game at the end of regulation, for which PFR assigns an equal likelihood of winning or losing in overtime).

This is the general pattern for preventing singular confidence at event horizons in any real-time decision engine, and it is the specific fix that let the modified PFR beat the random forest including overtime (.1511 vs .1522, p14).

Compare the upper-left and upper-right graphs in Figure 4 to see how this changes the time discounting function. This modified PFR model, which only allowed time to run down to 450 seconds, exhibited MSE = .1509.
